definitions.explanation: Protection against dust entering a device, space, or product. Used attributively (often as {防塵|ぼうじん}~) to describe products, masks, equipment, or rooms designed to keep dust out. Common on product specifications for cameras, smartphones, and industrial equipment.

examples.japanese: {防塵|ぼうじん}⟦マスク→マスク：05075_masuku⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦カメラ→カメラ：04417_kamera⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{防塵|ぼうじん}⟦{仕様|しよう}→仕様：00472_shiyou⟧だ。
⟦{工事現場|こうじげんば}→工事現場：26202_koujigenba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{防塵|ぼうじん}⟦ゴーグル→ゴーグル：07086_googuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: Dust-protection goggles are required on construction sites.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最新|さいしん}→最新：04831_saishin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スマートフォン→スマートフォン：04434_sumaatofon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{防水|ぼうすい}→防水：06428_bousui⟧・{防塵|ぼうじん}⟦{性能|せいのう}→性能：04340_seinou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}く→高い：00500_takai⟧、⟦アウトドア→アウトドア：10695_autodoa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{安心|あんしん}して→安心する：06067_anshinsuru⟧⟦{使|つか}える→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: The latest smartphones have high waterproof and dustproof performance, so you can use them outdoors with peace of mind.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{防|ぼう}→防〜：03967_bou⟧ (to prevent, to guard against) and {塵|じん} (dust). A technical term commonly seen on product labels, safety equipment, and industrial specifications.

USAGE:
{防塵|ぼうじん} is almost always used attributively — it modifies another noun rather than standing alone as a subject. On consumer electronics it very often appears paired with ⟦{防水|ぼうすい}→防水：06428_bousui⟧ (waterproof) as a single compact specification.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {防塵|ぼうじん}⟦マスク→マスク：05075_masuku⟧: dust mask
- {防塵|ぼうじん}⟦カバー→カバー：07812_kabaa⟧: dust cover
- {防塵|ぼうじん}⟦{仕様|しよう}→仕様：00472_shiyou⟧: dustproof design / specification
- {防塵|ぼうじん}⟦{性能|せいのう}→性能：04340_seinou⟧: dustproof performance
- ⟦{防水|ぼうすい}→防水：06428_bousui⟧・{防塵|ぼうじん}: waterproof and dustproof (a set phrase)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{防水|ぼうすい}→防水：06428_bousui⟧: waterproof — the parallel term for water resistance; the two are often paired
- {耐塵|たいじん}: dust-resistant — a less common variant emphasizing the ability to withstand dust rather than prevent its entry
- {集塵|しゅうじん}: dust collection — the opposite side of the problem, used for vacuum cleaners and industrial dust collectors
